gaps.sentence: I ___ the car tonight, so take a taxi into town.
gaps.hint: a future activity in progress as reason
gaps.explanation: The future continuous can express something in progress around a future time, here as a polite reason: will be using.

gaps.sentence: The neighbours ___ the flames with buckets for an hour by the time the firemen arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'For an hour by the time … arrived' — past perfect continuous for duration before a past moment.

gaps.sentence: The moon ___ round the Earth roughly every 27 days.
gaps.hint: a timeless fact about the moon
gaps.explanation: Timeless facts take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, with my phone switched off.
gaps.hint: this time next week means in progress
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous fits: will be lying.

gaps.sentence: Don't wake him — he has just ___ asleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Has just' is followed by the past participle: fallen.

gaps.sentence: The phone is ringing. Don't worry, I ___ it.
gaps.hint: a spontaneous decision at the moment
gaps.explanation: Decisions made at the moment of speaking use 'will': will answer.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry about the dog — it ___ at strangers, but it never bites.
gaps.hint: typical behavior takes the present simple
gaps.explanation: Characteristic, repeated behavior takes the present simple: barks.

gaps.sentence: Don't phone between seven and eight — we ___ dinner then.
gaps.hint: in progress at a stated future time
gaps.explanation: Something in progress at a stated future time takes the future continuous: will be having.
